title: vCenter Alarm Transitions to Yellow or Red
exclusions: Returns complete vCenter `AlarmStatusChangedEvent` records whose destination state is `yellow` or `red`, one row per vCenter event key. It does not reconstruct the current active-alarm inventory, prove the underlying condition still exists, identify a root cause, score vendor severity beyond the recorded state, correlate separate alarms into one incident, or detect alarms that were never configured, were disabled, were removed before collection, or occurred during a collection gap. Green and gray transitions remain available in raw retention but do not alert. Alarm definitions, acknowledgement, entity status, performance, topology, maintenance and source health are separate contracts. There is no count threshold: each qualifying transition is surfaced. This documentation-only rule changes no alarm, entity or vCenter setting and makes no availability or regulatory claim.
evidence: After deployment, retain governed vCenter/entity and alarm-definition inventories; add-on/DCN revisions and `event` task configuration; representative raw `vmware_inframon:events` records with eventClass, key, createdTime, alarm.name, entity.name/type, from, to, fullFormattedMessage, host/vCenter, `_time` and `_indextime`; independent event-pipeline and current-alarm reconciliation health; version-controlled `vcenter_alarm_degrading_transition`, ACL, schedule, dispatches and rows; maintenance/exception lookup history; incident disposition; and dated yellow, red, green, gray, blank-field, duplicate, delayed, wrong-source and collection-gap tests. This editorial review produced no vCenter event, active-alarm snapshot, Splunk execution, alert, incident, dashboard or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a fixed isolated event bucket, ingest two complete `vmware_inframon:events` fixtures with eventClass `vim.event.AlarmStatusChangedEvent`, distinct numeric keys, alarm names, entity names/types, `from=green`, and respectively `to=yellow` and `to=red`. Expect exactly two rows preserving both transitions, event identities, messages and times, with UC-2.1.13.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for `to=green`, `to=gray`, unrelated eventClass values, wrong index/sourcetype, blank event key, alarm name, entity name, or destination state, events outside the closed bucket, and exact replay of the same vCenter/key. A separate health/reconciliation test must expose a missing event task, stale vCenter, delayed records, schema drift and disagreement with the current triggered-alarm view.

dataSources: Primary source is vCenter Events API data collected by Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics with pool task `event` into the deployment-selected events index (documented default `index=vmware-taskevent`) and `sourcetype=vmware_inframon:events`. Required vSphere properties are event class, unique `key`, created time, `alarm.name`, `entity.name`, managed-entity type, `from`, `to`, `fullFormattedMessage`, and collector vCenter/host; `_time` and `_indextime` establish search and delay. Current triggered alarms, definitions, acknowledgement, topology, maintenance, and owner data are supporting sources.
app: Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (Splunkbase 5089) collects vCenter task/event API data through its scheduler and Data Collection Nodes. A local operations app owns the saved search, source-health and current-state reconciliation, maintenance lookup, dashboard, routing, tests and runbook.
spl:
index=vmware-taskevent sourcetype="vmware_inframon:events" eventClass="vim.event.AlarmStatusChangedEvent" earliest=-15m@m latest=-10m@m
| spath path=alarm.name output=alarm_name
| spath path=entity.name output=entity_name
| spath path=entity.entity.type output=entity_type
| eval vcenter=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(vcenter),""),nullif(trim(host),""))), event_key=trim(tostring(key)), old_status=lower(trim('from')), new_status=lower(trim('to'))
| where len(vcenter)>0 AND len(event_key)>0 AND len(alarm_name)>0 AND len(entity_name)>0 AND len(new_status)>0 AND in(new_status,"yellow","red")
| eval event_identity=vcenter."|".event_key
| dedup event_identity
| eval local_severity=if(new_status="red","high","medium"), use_case="UC-2.1.13", event_time=strftime(_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table _time vcenter event_key alarm_name entity_name entity_type old_status new_status local_severity fullFormattedMessage event_time _indextime use_case
| sort 0 -_time vcenter event_key
description: Surfaces each complete vCenter alarm-status event that moves an entity into yellow or red state during a closed five-minute event-time bucket. Results remain at unique vCenter event grain and preserve the alarm, entity, prior/new state and formatted message for reconciliation.
value: Consistent transition records let operations teams route deteriorating infrastructure conditions quickly and measure recurring alarm noise without scraping localized message text. Preserving event identity and state direction also helps distinguish new degradation from recovery, replay and stale active-alarm displays.
implementation: Enable the add-on's vCenter `event` collection, prove the nested AlarmStatusChangedEvent schema and independent pipeline health, then schedule the delayed nonoverlapping search every five minutes. Reconcile every result with current triggered alarms, topology and maintenance before escalation; never treat multiple alarms as one root cause without corroboration.
visualization: Use a transition table with event time, vCenter, alarm, entity/type, old/new state, local severity, message, indexing delay, maintenance, current-alarm state, owner and disposition. Add trends by alarm/entity and repeated transition pairs plus separate collection-health and unresolved-current-state panels. Avoid a single 'active alarms' count derived only from historical transitions.
schema: Native vSphere AlarmStatusChangedEvent JSON properties indexed as vmware_inframon:events
dataModelAcceleration: No published CIM dataset preserves vSphere alarm name, entity argument, transition direction and event key. Keep the raw event rule authoritative; summary indexing may support trends only after event-identity and state parity tests.

knownFalsePositives:
A matching event is a real recorded transition, but paging may be unnecessary after context review.

1. **Approved maintenance** — patching, evacuation, failover or device work can trigger expected alarms. Match exact entity, alarm and approved interval; retain the transition.

2. **Transient threshold crossing** — a short resource spike can move green→yellow→green. Inspect duration, underlying metric and recurrence rather than suppressing all recoveries.

3. **Cascading symptoms** — one datastore, network or host fault can trigger many VM alarms. Use topology and timing to group investigation while retaining each event; do not claim root cause from count.

4. **Stale or desynchronized alarm state** — vCenter can display a triggered alarm after the condition clears. Compare the current triggered-alarm view and alarm definition; preserve evidence of UI/state drift.

5. **Custom alarm semantics** — administrators can define different thresholds and actions. Resolve the exact alarm definition revision before assigning operational severity.

6. **Collector replay or overlap** — checkpoint reset, duplicate routes or overlapping windows can repeat keys. The rule deduplicates vCenter/key inside the bucket; health must identify recurrence across buckets.

7. **Entity rename or movement** — names and topology can change after the event. Use the event argument plus managed-object identity where available and current inventory, not name alone.

8. **Gray/unknown transitions** — excluded from paging by this rule but may indicate unavailable status or collection issues. Monitor them separately rather than relabeling them red.

**Suppression mechanism:** apply a governed post-result lookup keyed by vCenter, exact alarm name, stable entity identity and approved time interval, with owner, reason, ticket and finite expiry. Never discard raw transitions or suppress by all alarms on a cluster.

cost.search_load_notes: Five-minute bounded event search over one eventClass; current-state reconciliation is separate.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and semantic boundary

Assign vCenter, infrastructure-domain, Splunk and incident owners. Inventory governed vCenters, alarm definitions, entity ownership, maintenance calendars and routing. Broadcom defines AlarmStatusChangedEvent as a status change for an alarm; its object contains alarm and entity arguments plus `from` and `to`, while the base Event carries unique key, created time and formatted message. A transition is historical evidence, not a live alarm inventory or root-cause verdict.

## Step 1 — Collect and prove events

Deploy supported Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics components. Configure vCenter API access over TCP 443 with a read-only account and include `event` in `inframon_ta_vmware_pool.conf`. Verify output in the real events index; this contract uses the documented default `vmware-taskevent` and `vmware_inframon:events`.

Compare representative events with vSphere Client > Monitor > Tasks and Events and Triggered Alarms. Prove `eventClass=vim.event.AlarmStatusChangedEvent`, `key`, nested `alarm.name`, `entity.name`, `entity.entity.type`, `from`, `to`, `fullFormattedMessage`, vCenter/host, `_time` and `_indextime`. Keep the structured properties authoritative; messages can be localized. Build separate health for expected vCenters, event-task success/records_written, authentication, DCN workers, last event time across ordinary event classes, field completeness, delay, duplicate keys and clock drift. Quiet alarms do not imply broken collection.

## Step 2 — Save and schedule the SPL

Save the sidecar query as `vcenter_alarm_degrading_transition`, every five minutes. At 12:15 its `earliest=-15m@m latest=-10m@m` bucket covers 12:00 through but not including 12:05. Measure p99 event delay and move both bounds together if necessary; create a reviewed late-event reconciliation instead of overlapping schedules.

The base search fixes index, sourcetype, exact event class and closed range. `spath` extracts documented nested properties. Required-field checks prevent rows that cannot be investigated. Only destination yellow/red survives. Event identity is vCenter plus vSphere event key, not message text. Local severity maps red to high and yellow to medium for routing only; it is not a Broadcom severity or impact guarantee.

## Step 3 — Validate logic and current-state reconciliation

Use fixed JSON fixtures for every from/to combination among green, yellow, red and gray. Test two alarms on one entity, one alarm on two entities, same key on different vCenters, duplicate key on one vCenter, blank nested fields, localized messages, rename, delayed/future time, wrong eventClass/source and rerun. Assert no count threshold or root-cause label appears.

In a nonproduction vCenter, use owner-approved benign alarm thresholds to cause and clear yellow/red transitions. Compare API event key/time/properties, vSphere Client history, current Triggered Alarms and Splunk. Do not induce host, datastore or production failure. Verify acknowledgement and alarm reset do not get confused with the recorded condition transition.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and respond

Route by exact alarm definition and entity owner. Include raw structured fields, event/index time and delay, current state, maintenance, topology, related metrics/events and a restricted vCenter link. Triage: verify record/source; inspect alarm definition and transition; reconcile current status; correlate entity dependencies and contemporaneous metrics; identify maintenance/change; then assign root-cause investigation. Close only with documented disposition, current state and healthy collection.

Do not reset alarms, disable definitions, migrate/power VMs, enter maintenance, restart services or change thresholds automatically from this row. Those actions require domain evidence, approval and rollback.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- No events: verify pool `event` task, vCenter credentials/443, scheduler/DCN/forwarding, index/RBAC and independent common-event health.
- Null alarm/entity: inspect raw JSON, add-on version, truncation and `spath`; do not parse the localized message as the sole fallback.
- Duplicate rows: compare vCenter/key, windows, collector checkpoints and routes.
- Persistent active alarm but no new row: expected when no new transition occurred; use current-alarm reconciliation.
- Many alarms at once: inspect shared host/datastore/network topology before paging each symptom independently.
- State differs from UI: align event time, current-state query time, acknowledgement/reset, alarm-definition revision and vCenter clock.

Keep status draft until production owners sign off source coverage, fixtures, routing and safe response. Documentation review is not runtime validation.
grandmaExplanation: We show when the virtualization manager says an alarm has changed into a warning or serious state. The team still checks whether the problem is current and what actually caused it before taking action.
hardware: vCenter-managed datacenters, clusters, hosts, virtual machines, datastores, networks and other managed entities with configured vSphere alarms.
